entries.reason: This paper reveals a fundamentally new interphasic engineering mechanism driven by the reduction-induced structural distortion of fluorinated aromatic additives, which significantly enhances the interphasic stability of sodium-ion batteries.
entries.title: Unlocking Sodium-Ion Batteries' Potential
entries.paragraph: Researchers have discovered a new mechanism to enhance the stability of sodium-ion batteries. They found that adding a specific type of aromatic additive to the battery's anode can create a protective layer that prevents the battery from degrading over time. This layer, called a solid electrolyte interphase, is crucial for maintaining the battery's performance and safety. The team's findings could lead to the development of more efficient and reliable sodium-ion batteries.

entries.reason: This study demonstrates a molecular-level surface design that actively orchestrates an anionic bottom-up flux from the electrolyte bulk to the hard carbon interface, fundamentally redirecting the electrolyte decomposition and improving the stability of sodium-ion batteries.
entries.title: Designing Better Anodes for Sodium-Ion Batteries
entries.paragraph: Scientists have developed a new way to design the surface of hard carbon anodes in sodium-ion batteries. By creating a specific pattern of chemical groups on the surface, they can control the flow of ions and prevent the battery from degrading. This approach leads to improved performance and stability, with the battery retaining 96.5% of its capacity after 5,000 cycles.

entries.reason: This work proposes a surfactant-mediated microemulsion electrolyte strategy that effectively protects the internal anion-induced ion–solvent-coordinated structure, while the microemulsion retains low viscosity and high ionic conductivity, addressing the major safety risks of conventional carbonate electrolytes in sodium-ion batteries.
entries.title: Safer Sodium-Ion Batteries through Microemulsion Electrolytes
entries.paragraph: Researchers have developed a new type of electrolyte that can improve the safety of sodium-ion batteries. By creating a microemulsion of two liquids, they can create a stable and efficient electrolyte that prevents the battery from overheating or catching fire. The team's findings could lead to the development of safer and more reliable sodium-ion batteries.

entries.reason: This critical review links molecular-scale electrolyte solvation and interphase chemistry to electrode compatibility, full-cell engineering, manufacturing constraints, and commercial viability, providing a comprehensive understanding of the key factors that influence the performance and sustainability of sodium-ion batteries.
entries.title: The State of Sodium-Ion Batteries: A Critical Review
entries.paragraph: This review paper provides an in-depth look at the current state of sodium-ion batteries. The authors compare different types of electrolytes and electrodes, and discuss the challenges and opportunities for this emerging technology. They also highlight the importance of understanding the molecular-scale interactions between the electrolyte and the electrodes, and the need for further research to improve the performance and safety of sodium-ion batteries.

entries.reason: This study presents a comprehensive electrochemical and electromechanical characterization of commercial 18650 sodium-ion battery cells, establishing a foundational understanding of their behavior across a wide range of operating conditions and providing a critical gap in the literature regarding their performance and safety characteristics.
entries.title: Understanding the Impedance of Sodium-Ion Batteries
entries.paragraph: Researchers have conducted a comprehensive study of the impedance of commercial sodium-ion batteries. They used a technique called electrochemical impedance spectroscopy to measure the battery's performance under different conditions, including varying temperatures and states of charge. The team's findings provide valuable insights into the behavior of sodium-ion batteries and could inform the development of more efficient and reliable battery management systems.
